newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds slip hand in hand with Germany.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds slip hand in hand with Germany.

text.p: 1555 GMT - Austrian bonds corrected down on Wednesday in line with the German market after surprisingly strong jump in the Ifo index.
But traders said sentiment remains buoyant despite correction.
"Market direction now hinges on Treasuries," said one trader, adding today's correction is just seen as the market taking a breather.
"The overall scenario remains basically bullish," said another.
Traders cited demand above all in the short end.
* Latest 10 year benchmark 5.875 pct bond maturing July 2006 down 15 bps at 99.65 to yield 5.92 (5.90) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 99.48/58 to yield 5.94/93.
* At the near end, five-year 5.50 percent bond maturing March 2001 down 10 bps at 102.85 to yield 4.79 (4.76) percent in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 102.70/80 to yield 4.82/80 percent.
* 10-year spread to German bunds steady at 11 bps, five-year spread up three at 20 bps.
* December AGB future down 37 bps at 106.78 on volume of 459 contracts.
* Money market rates mixed with three-month VIBOR a shade higher at 3.322 and overnight money steady at 3.04/29. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
